account: Udbetaling Danmark (UDK), the Danish public authority that has centralized welfare payments since 2012, has its benefits administered by ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension). ATP designs the fraud-control components of UDK's Joint Data Unit (Den Faelles Dataenhed), which the University of Copenhagen's Offentlig AI database says was established in 2014. NNIT A/S is the supplier. The registry describes profiling and machine learning run on linked register data, and it names Naive Bayes classification and cluster analysis. Background sources give earlier yields. In July 2019 the Danish legal think tank Justitia used UDK figures to show that UDK's data-based controls led to 705 cases in 2017 and 1,094 cases in 2018 with benefits stopped, changed or repaid. Its author argues that this yield is very low for data matching that can cover up to 2.7 million recipients. The Automating Society 2020 Denmark chapter cites the July 2019 report and gives the same counts out of 2.7 million screened beneficiaries. AlgorithmWatch (2020) reports that controls in 2017 and 2018 unveiled about half a billion kroner in erroneous payments. As of 2019 UDK was reported to use up to 60 algorithms for fraud detection and other purposes. In a letter to Amnesty International before November 2024, UDK supplied its 2023 statistics for three data-driven controls. The 2023 figures carry no day. The “Really Single” model produced 412 requested cases, 292 established control cases and 135 cases with revenue (benefits stopped or reduced). “Model Abroad” (unreported departures, state and disability pension) gave 511, 351 and 36. The parental-leave controls including the “Fictitious Employment” model gave 491, 207 and 72. UDK cautioned that cases with revenue in a year are not necessarily a proportion of cases established that year. On 11 January 2024 a UDK and ATP control official told Amnesty that the team manages 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year, of which around 1,800 come from the models. A freedom-of-information report on dm.dk in October 2024 said that nearly all 1.2 million pensioners were screened and that only 36 cases in 2023 ended with a benefit stopped or reduced. That matches the Model Abroad row. The dm.dk report is not among the cited sources, and neither is ATP's page, which credits 260 million kr. a year of savings to IT modernization generally. Amnesty's report of 12 November 2024 concludes that it is questionable whether the algorithms are effective. It finds that most opened cases end with no further action. It also finds that the system risks discrimination and mass surveillance. A Copenhagen Municipality control official said that more often than not there is no fraud in the cases that UDK sends. Amnesty's report states that the Danish Data Protection Authority told it that it acts only on inquiries or complaints. No regulator finding on the models is on record.

ai_role.statement: The models select “requested cases” that UDK's HOK control team screens and investigates. Decisions to stop or reduce benefits are taken by humans after investigation. UDK measures model quality by the share of cases the team accepts for manual processing. Every outcome figure is a UDK statement (FOI responses and a letter) as reproduced verbatim in Amnesty International's report. No official publication of them is among the sources. Amnesty contests effectiveness and alleges discrimination risks, and UDK rejected parts of Amnesty's assessment. NNIT built the models to ATP's specifications. No developer-authored source is on record. The dm.dk report and ATP's page are not among the sources.

fields.account: Udbetaling Danmark (UDK), the Danish public authority that has centralized welfare payments since 2012, has its benefits administered by ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension). ATP designs the fraud-control components of UDK's Joint Data Unit (Den Faelles Dataenhed), which the University of Copenhagen's Offentlig AI database says was established in 2014. NNIT A/S is the supplier. The registry describes profiling and machine learning run on linked register data, and it names Naive Bayes classification and cluster analysis. Background sources give earlier yields. In July 2019 the Danish legal think tank Justitia used UDK figures to show that UDK's data-based controls led to 705 cases in 2017 and 1,094 cases in 2018 with benefits stopped, changed or repaid. Its author argues that this yield is very low for data matching that can cover up to 2.7 million recipients. The Automating Society 2020 Denmark chapter cites the July 2019 report and gives the same counts out of 2.7 million screened beneficiaries. AlgorithmWatch (2020) reports that controls in 2017 and 2018 unveiled about half a billion kroner in erroneous payments. As of 2019 UDK was reported to use up to 60 algorithms for fraud detection and other purposes. In a letter to Amnesty International before November 2024, UDK supplied its 2023 statistics for three data-driven controls. The 2023 figures carry no day. The “Really Single” model produced 412 requested cases, 292 established control cases and 135 cases with revenue (benefits stopped or reduced). “Model Abroad” (unreported departures, state and disability pension) gave 511, 351 and 36. The parental-leave controls including the “Fictitious Employment” model gave 491, 207 and 72. UDK cautioned that cases with revenue in a year are not necessarily a proportion of cases established that year. On 11 January 2024 a UDK and ATP control official told Amnesty that the team manages 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year, of which around 1,800 come from the models. A freedom-of-information report on dm.dk in October 2024 said that nearly all 1.2 million pensioners were screened and that only 36 cases in 2023 ended with a benefit stopped or reduced. That matches the Model Abroad row. The dm.dk report is not among the cited sources, and neither is ATP's page, which credits 260 million kr. a year of savings to IT modernization generally. Amnesty's report of 12 November 2024 concludes that it is questionable whether the algorithms are effective. It finds that most opened cases end with no further action. It also finds that the system risks discrimination and mass surveillance. A Copenhagen Municipality control official said that more often than not there is no fraud in the cases that UDK sends. Amnesty's report states that the Danish Data Protection Authority told it that it acts only on inquiries or complaints. No regulator finding on the models is on record.

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary of the controls is identified. The people directly affected are those investigated. By Amnesty's reading of UDK's figures, 54% to almost 90% of opened cases per model ended with no further action.

UDK's own 2023 figures give 135, 36 and 72 cases with revenue from three models against 412, 511 and 491 requested cases. No amounts are given, and the authority says that yearly figures are not directly comparable.

No societal outcome is reported beyond the cases with revenue that UDK counts for itself. The 2023 figures give no amounts, so the extent of any gain to public funds cannot be established, and Amnesty's report questions whether the models are effective.

purpose: Built to flag benefit recipients at elevated risk of receiving unentitled payments for manual control by UDK's control team. The recorded outcome, cases with benefits stopped or reduced, is that purpose.

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary of the controls is identified. The people directly affected are those investigated. By Amnesty's reading of UDK's figures, 54% to almost 90% of opened cases per model ended with no further action.

UDK's own 2023 figures give 135, 36 and 72 cases with revenue from three models against 412, 511 and 491 requested cases. No amounts are given, and the authority says that yearly figures are not directly comparable.

No societal outcome is reported beyond the cases with revenue that UDK counts for itself. The 2023 figures give no amounts, so the extent of any gain to public funds cannot be established, and Amnesty's report questions whether the models are effective.
